summary.oneLiner: Gujarat Containers Limited is a Gujarat-based iron-and-steel-consuming manufacturer operating its own manufacturing facilities (including the Savli Plant), whose sales volume decreased around 3.91% in FY2025-26.
summary.business: The Company is a single-business manufacturer whose key procurement input is iron and steel, produced at its own manufacturing facilities including the Savli Plant. Selling prices track raw-material prices: revenue from operations fell 3.93% in 2025-26 because a reduction in raw material prices flowed through into lower product sales prices, with sales volume down around 3.91%. It is a stand-alone entity with no subsidiary, associate or joint venture, carries out no research and development, has imported no technology, and reported no inflow or outflow of foreign exchange during the year.

endMarkets: India / domestic only - the Company reported no inflow or outflow of foreign exchange during FY2025-26, and procures raw materials from domestic suppliers located in different parts of the country

currentContext.expansion: The only expansion disclosed in the routed text is an energy asset rather than added manufacturing capacity: the Company has installed a solar power plant at its Savli Plant 'to promote the use of renewable energy and reduce dependence on conventional sources of power', at a capital investment of Rs. 123.33 Lakhs. The Directors' Report is internally inconsistent on its output - one line states that 'During the financial year under review, the solar power plant generated approximately 11,14,367 units of electricity, resulting in reduced grid power consumption', while the following line states the plant 'generated solar Electricity of 1,80,000 units during the Financial Year 2024-25'. No installed solar MW rating is given. Beyond this, there was no change in the nature of the business, no subsidiary, associate or joint venture was formed, no loans, guarantees or investments in other body corporates were made, no scrapped plant and machinery was sold in FY 2025-26, and the Company states 'There were no material changes that have affected the financial position of the Company which have occurred between the end of financial year on 31st March, 2026 and till the date of this report.' The MD&A notes that gross fixed assets including leasehold land, plant and machinery decreased year on year, and the Company confirms it has taken no new technology for absorption and carries out no research and development activities. No new plant, line, debottlenecking or commissioning timeline is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

risks.risk: Availability of raw materials, more particularly iron and steel
risks.note: Listed first under MD&A 'Risks and concerns' as a key procurement-relationship risk; the Company's only stated mitigation is planning well in advance to procure from reputed domestic suppliers located in different parts of the country
'the price of raw materials may be subject to material changes in world-wide pricing levels' - as an iron-and-steel converter the Company is a price-taker on its principal input

risks.risk: Selling prices track input prices, so input deflation directly shrinks revenue
risks.note: Management attributes the FY2025-26 decline itself to this pass-through: revenue from operations fell 3.93% because 'reduction in the raw material prices ... caused reduction in sales prices of the product', with sales volume down around 3.91% - the mechanism means margins, not just prices, ride the steel cycle

risks.risk: Very high non-material input costs - freight and electricity
risks.note: Explicitly flagged in MD&A 'Risks and concerns' alongside frequent fluctuation in raw material prices in the market; the Savli solar plant is the only disclosed structural offset to the electricity leg

risks.risk: Key supplier concentration and contract-renewal risk
risks.note: 'key supplier relationships may be lost or impaired, contracts renewed on less favorable terms or exit of key suppliers from the market' - a stated dependence on a small set of procurement relationships

The MD&A opens on 'continued geopolitical conflicts between Russia-Ukraine War, Israel and Palestine war, Iran & Israel attack and modest global growth' as the backdrop against which domestic demand has carried growth
The only company-relevant caveat in the Outlook: 'Even outlook looks positive in FY 2026-27, the recent rapid rate hike may have impact on credit'

Structural concentration disclosed rather than labelled as risk: no change in the nature of business, no subsidiary, associate or joint venture, no research and development activity and no technology absorbed, and 'There was no inflow or outflow of foreign exchange, during the year under review' - i.e. no export or overseas diversification of the revenue base
